rows.why: What sets this scenario apart is the day unit: "2d" gives 172800000 and "1d0h0m0s0ms" gives 86400000. Item 5 asks whether days are supported. Its pick supports only h/m/s/ms and rejects "1d". Item 8 (zero components) also fits the "0s" rows, but the day rows are the main point.

Item 4 asks whether whitespace is allowed in a duration string. The scenario trims leading and trailing whitespace and accepts "  45m\n". The pick allows no spaces at all, so it would reject this input.

Most of the rejected rows are about whitespace, signs, decimals or non-ASCII digits: "1.5h", "-3s", "+3s", "1h 30m", "3 s" and "３s" (full-width digit). Item 4 asks that exact question. Its pick rejects all of them, which matches. Items 1, 3, 5 and 7 each cover one row but fit less well.
Item 9 asks whether a component can exceed the next unit, such as "100m". The pick accepts any count and sums it, so "90m" gives 5400000 as expected.
Item 2 asks about unit order and repeats. The pick requires a fixed order with each unit at most once and rejects "30m1h" and "1m1m". That matches rejecting the out-of-order and repeated rows.
Item 6 asks about the upper limit. The pick caps at 2^53-1 inclusive, so exactly 9007199254740991 is accepted. The input uses "d", which item 5's pick rejects, but that is a separate question.
Item 6 asks what happens above the limit. The pick raises ValueError above 2^53-1, which is what the scenario expects for these rows.

Most rows test greedy output with the largest units first: 5400000 gives "1h30m" and 86400000 gives "1d". Item 10's pick looks for the shortest string and prints "90m" for 5400000. Item 11 covers the 0 row, and its pick "0s" also disagrees with the expected "0ms".

The expected output "104249991d8h59m991ms" is the greedy one and is 20 characters. A shortest-string search would print something else, such as "2501999792h59m991ms" at 19 characters. Item 5's pick also cannot print "d" at all.
No item asks whether formatting a value and parsing the result gives the same number back. That is a consistency property, not one of the open questions.
Item 12 asks how the formatter handles negative, bool, float and above-maximum input. The pick raises ValueError for all of them, matching the rows -1, 2^53, True and 1.0.
